name: Boom Supersonic
summary: Boom Supersonic is developing Overture, a proposed supersonic airliner, after flying its XB-1 demonstrator. Its investment case is a long-duration bet on certification, manufacturing and demand for premium-speed travel.
overview: Boom Supersonic is developing Overture, a proposed supersonic airliner, and has used its XB-1 demonstrator to test core technologies. The company sits at the intersection of aerospace certification, advanced manufacturing and premium commercial aviation.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.value: Series B-1 at a reported $1.5B–$1.8B valuation
facts.note: Reported valuation range for Boom's Series B-1 financing.

bull_case: A successful Overture program could reopen a premium aviation category that has had no commercial successor to Concorde. Progress on engines, airline orders and a scalable production system would materially de-risk the thesis.
bear_case: Civil certification, engine development and factory ramp are capital-intensive and unusually difficult. A reported secondary valuation range is not a substitute for evidence of a completed priced round or commercial delivery.
latest_round: Series B-1 at a reported $1.5B–$1.8B valuation
directory_notes: XB-1 demonstrator flown; Overture remains in development.

intelligence.description: Boom designs a proposed supersonic airliner and the systems required to bring it to market.
company: Boom Supersonic is building Overture, a proposed Mach 1.7 commercial airliner, alongside the manufacturing and propulsion program needed to certify it. Its XB-1 demonstrator has provided a visible technology milestone, but Overture still faces the far harder work of commercial certification and industrial ramp.

The company disclosed a $100 million Series B in 2019 and says it has raised more than $700 million of investment and other capital. A $1.5 billion to $1.8 billion Series B-1 valuation has been reported by private-market data providers, rather than announced by Boom as a completed priced transaction.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Boom is a useful test of whether private capital can finance a clean-sheet commercial aircraft program outside established aerospace primes. Its progress also matters for suppliers, airports and airlines considering a return of premium supersonic routes.

changed.text: XB-1 completed a supersonic flight, a key demonstrator milestone before Overture certification.

takeaways: The central question is whether Boom can convert a flight-test program into a certifiable, economically viable airliner.
Reported private-market pricing should be treated as indicative until a completed transaction is directly substantiated.
Engine, certification and production milestones are more decision-useful than headline valuation alone.
